record.paper_title: Open problems in theory of metric linear spaces
record.context_brief: Continuous linear functionals on nuclear F-spaces
record.original_question: In every nuclear F-space, must there exist a nontrivial continuous linear functional?

evidence.quote: PROBLEM 10. - Do in each nuclear F-space non trivial linear continuous functionals exist ?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
An F-space is a topological vector space whose topology is induced by a complete translation-invariant metric (equivalently, by an F-norm). Such a space is not assumed to be locally convex. A notion of nuclearity can be defined for general (not necessarily locally convex) F-spaces, for instance via the existence, for every neighborhood U of 0, of another neighborhood V of 0 such that the canonical map between the associated quotient/completion spaces is a nuclear operator in an appropriate metric-linear sense.

Question: Does every nuclear F-space E admit a nontrivial continuous linear functional, i.e., a continuous linear map f : E → ℝ (or ℂ) with f ≢ 0?

Equivalently: is it impossible for a nuclear F-space to have trivial topological dual {0}?
artifact.category_tag: Nuclear F-spaces and continuous linear functionals
artifact.status_search_result: Web searches did not return a definitive resolution of this question. Standard references treat nuclear spaces in the locally convex setting (where the Hahn–Banach theorem trivially yields nontrivial continuous linear functionals), while there exist non-locally-convex F-spaces (such as L^p for 0 < p < 1) whose continuous dual is trivial. No clear published source was found confirming whether the question for nuclear F-spaces in the non-locally-convex sense has been settled.

status_evidence.title: Nuclear space - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: Nuclear spaces are typically defined as Hausdorff locally convex spaces such that every continuous linear map into a Banach space is nuclear.
status_evidence.claim: Standard literature treats nuclearity in the locally convex setting, leaving the non-locally-convex F-space case outside mainstream references.

status_evidence.title: Linear form - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: There exist topological vector spaces, such as L^p for 0 < p < 1, whose only continuous linear functional is the zero functional.
status_evidence.claim: Non-locally-convex F-spaces with trivial dual exist in general, motivating the question for the nuclear subclass.
